comparison: Both evaluate the identification of mAZ and sAZ inputs (C4, C29-C33, C80-C82). OpenEval finds these claims well-supported by STORM and EM data. Peer reviewers also accept this as a 'valuable analysis' and 'foundational descriptive finding without challenge.' Strong agreement on support.

Both address eye-specific differences in mAZ input density and fraction (C5-C6, C25, C35-C37, C83). OpenEval finds these supported by quantitative STORM data with statistical significance. Peer reviewers acknowledge statistical significance but express uncertainty about biological relevance due to 'small effect sizes,' questioning whether differences are 'informative regarding this biological question.' Disagreement on biological significance.

Both evaluate sAZ synapse density equalization claims (C7, C27, C38-C40, C89). OpenEval finds these supported as a 'key developmental transition.' Peer reviewers note consistency across groups but express uncertainty due to 'small effect sizes' and concerns that 'estimates of standard deviation—and therefore effect size—are unreliable' with only three experiments. Disagreement on strength of support.

Both address β2KO phenotype findings (C8-C9, C28, C41-C42, C101-C104). OpenEval finds these supported by quantitative data showing maintained mAZ formation but reduced sAZ density. Peer reviewers also support this, describing it as 'useful information about the development' and acknowledging 'changes in synapse density and in the occurrence of multi-active zone synapses.' Strong agreement on support.

Both evaluate vesicle pool size differences (C43-C49, with C23, C26 in OpenEval only). OpenEval finds these supported by VGluT2 volume measurements showing significant eye-specific differences. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, acknowledging the measurements but emphasizing concerns about 'small effect sizes' and questioning biological relevance. Disagreement on biological significance.

Both address vesicle pool scaling with AZ number (C50-C52, C56-C59, C84). OpenEval finds strong support from correlation analysis (r=0.99 for WT). Peer reviewers also support this as part of 'first order analysis' showing proportionality, treating it as a 'descriptive finding without challenge.' Strong agreement on support.

Partial overlap on AZ number differences between eyes (C53-C55). OpenEval includes these in broader scaling analysis and finds them supported. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, applying their general concerns about 'small effect sizes' and reliability of estimates with limited experiments. Disagreement on strength of support.

Both evaluate spatial clustering analysis (C63-C71, C90). OpenEval finds these well-supported by clustering analysis with appropriate statistical methods. Peer reviewers acknowledge the clustering characterization but express uncertainty, noting 'small effect sizes' and that authors have 'tempered' earlier causal interpretations, questioning biological significance. Disagreement on biological significance.

Both address distance measurements between clustered and isolated inputs (C72-C77, C92). OpenEval finds these supported with appropriate statistical analysis. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, applying concerns about 'small effect sizes' and noting that 'estimates of standard deviation—and therefore effect size—are unreliable' with limited experiments. Disagreement on strength of support.

Both evaluate the lack of vesicle pool differences between near and far sAZ synapses (C78-C79). OpenEval finds this negative result supported. Peer reviewers also accept this as a 'straightforward observation' without challenge. Strong agreement on support.

Both address the main summary conclusions about eye-specific differences (C10, C87). OpenEval finds these well-supported by collective findings. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting that 'revisions improve presentation but do not substantively resolve the difficulty in drawing strong conclusions from the data set' and that authors have 'tempered' earlier causal interpretations. Disagreement on strength of mechanistic conclusions.
OpenEval evaluates background/prior knowledge claims (C1-C3, C12-C18) as well-supported by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background context claims.

OpenEval evaluates literature-based mechanistic context claims (C19-C22, C60-C61, C86, C88, C96, C98-C100, C105-C108) as supported by cited literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature summary claims.

OpenEval evaluates speculative interpretations (C62, C91, C94-C95, C97, C109) as uncertain, noting they are appropriately presented as possibilities requiring validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific speculative claims.

OpenEval evaluates the study limitation about inability to determine single vs. multiple RGC axons (C93) as appropriately identified. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific limitation.

OpenEval evaluates comparative analysis with other developmental systems (C110-C122) as supported by citations, though noting the conserved mechanism proposal remains somewhat speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these comparative claims.

OpenEval evaluates validation of eye-specific assignments (C34) as supported by control experiments from prior publication. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this methodological validation claim.
